data.name: Entitled
data.detailed_description:
You come from Nayas - a tribe famous for its fierce warriors. You arrived in the Tabehoudai Kingdom to save it from the evil Ganomort. You defeat him. The king is relieved. The princess cheers. You're about to be announced the hero... And then you wake up.

It’s your graduation day. You have no money. No roof over your head and a degree in Management that apparently isn’t even enough to get a job at the farm. Joining the Heroes Guild doesn’t seem likely anytime soon. Will you be able to break the 9 to 5 loop and become a hero? Will you rebel against the reality that seems to be designed against you? Or maybe you’ll find solace in calm repetition...

Entitled might feel like any other retro-jRPG at first, but that couldn't be further from the truth. Sure, you can finish the game by defeating the evil Ganomort and rescuing the Princess. But there’s countless ways to go off the beaten path… and not one of them is obvious.

The world of Entitled is a quirky mix of fantasy and real life. Modern economic themes blend with a medieval fantasy setting. One moment you’re delivering swords for the blacksmith, hoping someday you will own a sword of your own and become a proper hero. Shortly after, you pay taxes and attend lectures on supply and demand on the job market. All that to figure out what to actually do with your mediocre life.

If you want to beat the game, you have to first confront your biggest enemy: the misguided notion that you’re special.

Features

  • An economy that feels uncomfortably familiar.

  • Whole hidden storylines, areas and dungeons.

  • Hundreds of more or less obscure pop culture references.

  • Two combat systems, even though they don't really matter.

  • A wide range of nods to the 90s gaming. Of course the princess will turn out to be a party member, a love interest and a healer!

  • The most realistic fishing simulation ever seen in games.

data.short_description: Finally, a game you deserve! It's entirely up to you whether you save the princess or rob the bank. But can you actually find a way to make it happen? Entitled is a young adult simulator in a modern medieval fantasy world, with a lot of secret content.
data.reviews:
“[...] that’s kind of the game’s brilliance. The game has rules, but also provides players with the tools to break them. It puts players in charge of their own moral compass. The problem is between it is forcing the player to slog through the slow bits to get to the interesting bits. These days it’s a challenge to get a player to do that.”
Versus Evil

“It's nothing like Disco Elysium. Look at Disco Elysium. Why didn't you make a game like Disco Elysium? More games should be like Disco Elysium.”
Team 17

“It crosses red lines that make this game unpublishable in this day and age.”
All in! Games

content_descriptors.notes:
There's nothing really graphic. Just cartoonish violence without blood, no nudity.

There are some themes that can be considered mature though. You can visit a night club for example. Or you can try to pick up girls, sometimes with lines that are a bit crass. Nothing graphic, vulgar or explicit, but still probably not for little kids. 

The whole game revolves around economy and being a young adult trying to find his place in society so in a way, that's also a "mature topic".
